mekayis.metin:
(قَبَوَ) الْقَافُ وَالْبَاءُ وَالْوَاوُ كَلِمَةٌ صَحِيحَةٌ، تَدُلُّ عَلَى ضَمٍّ وَجَمْعٍ. يُقَالُ: قَبَوْتُ الشَّيْءَ: جَمَعْتُهُ وَضَمَمْتُهُ. وَأَهْلُ الْمَدِينَةِ يُسَمُّونَ الرَّفْعَ فِي الْحَرَكَاتِ قَبْوًا. وَهَذَا حَرْفٌ مَقْبُوٌّ. وَيُقَالُ: إِنَّ الْقَبَاءَ مُشْتَقٌّ مِنْهُ، لِأَنَّ الْإِنْسَانَ يَجْمَعُهُ عَلَى نَفْسِهِ.
[بَابُ الْقَافِ وَالتَّاءِ وَمَا يَثْلُثُهُمَا]

( ʕan from) | se cacher (cf. ↗QBʕ)’: † ĭnqabà (VII) ▪ † QBW_9 ‘ventricule (d’un ruminant)’: † qib(b)aẗ see ↗ † QBː (QBB)_13 ▪ † QBW_10 ʻwine-drinkers | buveurs de vin qui boivent en compagnie’: † banū qābiyāʔᵃ ▪ † QBW_11 ‘desert’: † qabāyaẗ ▪ † QBW_12 ‘fat | gras, chargé de graisse (homme)’: † maqbīy ▪ † QBW_13 † …: ‘…’ ▪ [v1] (Rolland2014:) According to Nişanyan, the Ar qabāʔ ‘outer garment with full-length sleeves’ is from (Tietze2016: akin to) Aram ḳbāyā ‘id.’, but else a typical Wanderwort (cf. Lat capa etc., see below, section WEST). – Some authors assume a relation to the root √QBW (↗ qabā ‘to vault, arch, camber, curve, bend’). – Influence by, or on, Ar ↗ ǧubbaẗ and ↗ ʕabāʔ ? Semantic overlapping and interference is not unlikely. ▪ [v2] : The main item here is prob. not the vb. qabā but the n. qabw ‘vault, arch, cave, underground room’, interestingly also ‘testudo, besieging machine | sorte de machine de guerre sous laquelle les assiégeants s’abritaient en approchant des murs d’une place forte’. The word has no direct cognates, but is certainly akin to ↗QBː (QBB)_5 and ↗ qubbaẗ ‘vaulted room, vaulted tent, (etc.)’. – Semantic proximity between both qabw and qubbaẗ , on the one hand, and Eg kꜣp.t , Dem ḳp ‘covers (of the sky)’ > Copt kēpe ( čēpe , čepē ) ‘vaulted place, cellar, canopy’ (Crum1939, Westendorf2008), on the other, could let one speculate about a possible relation also here. The same holds for Akk kapāpu ( kabābu ) ‘to bend, curve, wrap around (tr.); to bend, curve (intr.)’ (adj. kuppupu ‘bent, bowed’) and kabābu ( gabābu ) ‘shield’ (Akk loanword in Sum!) although Akk / p / should correspond to Ar / f /, not / b /, and one would have to explain the shift from Akk / k / to Ar / q / in ¹ qabā ‘to bent, bow’. 1 Influence of semantically close ↗ qubbaẗ ? ▪ † [v3] : A similar mismatch as in [v2] between the Ar evidence and what may suggest itself, semantically, as possible cognate can be observed with Ar † ² qabā ( u , qabw ) ‘to pluck, take off s.th. with the fingers; to collect (saffron)’ and Syr qəp̄ā ‘to collect, gather in heaps’. If not this item, no other “cognates” are around. – On another note, should one connect the ‘plucking, collecting’ of this value to that of ‘bowing, bending’ of [v2]? The vb.s look completely identical… – as they also do in values † [v4] and † [v5]… ▪ † [v4]– † [v11]: There is conspicuous formal identity between [v2] ¹ qabā ‘to bend, bow, vault, arch’, † [v3] † ² qabā ‘to pluck, collect (saffron)’, † [v4] † ³ qabā ‘to raise (a building)’ and † [v5] † ⁴ qabā ‘disperser’. But what could be a common semantic denominator (which also might help to identify possible cognates, if any)? The situation gets even more complicated and puzzling when we include values † [v6] to † [v11] into the consideration: each of these add a new dimension that does not seem to have anything to do with any of the other values. ▪ † [v9] : † qibaẗ ‘(sheep) tripes, ventricle (of a lamb, a ruminant)’ is often listed s.r. √QBW, but may actually be from ↗√WQB *‘cavity’ (WQB_1) or, as the variant † qibbaẗ can suggest, from ↗ † QBː (QBB) (see #13). ▪ † [v10] : Is the strange * FāʕiLāʔᵘ pattern a mere poetic “exaggeration” of an underlying PA.f, * qābiyaẗ , so that the † banū qābiyāʔᵃ ʻwine-drinkers’ would be *‘those of the vaulted (room), i.e., the tavern’? ▪ † [v11]– † [v12] : Are † qabāyaẗ ‘desert’ and † maqbīy ‘fat’ perh. from another root (↗√QBY)? But even if so, what could be a common semantic denominator? ▪ … 1 . Cf. Dolgopolsky2012 #847 Nostr * kib˅ ‘hump, bend; to bend’ > NaIE * gei̯bʰ- ‘hump, bend’ > Lat gibbus ‘hump, hunch’ ( gībus ), gibber ‘hump-backed’ || Sem *√KPP ‘to bend’ (× Nostr * ḲupE [or * Ḳüp˅ ] ‘to bend’) > Akk, mHbr, JudAram, Syr √KPP ‘to bend’, Syr kəp̄īp̄-ā ‘hump’, kəp̄īp̄ūṯ-ā ‘crookedness’, JudAram, Syr √KPW/Y, kəp̄ā ‘to bent, bow, incline, lean over’, ?
